headline: Why Correct Software Resists Proof
lede: Gödel, Rice, and the halting problem draw a hard perimeter around software verification. Formal methods remain powerful, but every proof spends computational effort and rests on assumptions that complex systems may not honor.

headline: The Tutor That Refuses To Tell
lede: Jane Street’s Socratic Tutor turns an AI assistant into a patient examiner. It maps what a learner can demonstrate, advances one question at a time, and treats mastery as something earned rather than declared.

headline: Boot Logs Become A Living Tree
lede: Bootvine replaces systemd’s blur of scrolling messages with a live Rust-rendered tree. Pending jobs, slow units, prompts, and failures become visible at the moment they matter.

headline: Remembering Tim Peters, In Code And Spirit
lede: Tim Peters helped give Python both its sorting algorithm and its moral vocabulary. His patience, technical judgment, and Zen of Python shaped a language whose community will continue to carry his imprint.

headline: When Paint Splatters Compile As Perl
lede: A SIGBOVIK paper feeds paint splatters through OCR and asks Perl to make sense of them. Ninety-three percent parse successfully, which is either an empirical result or an exceptionally committed joke.

headline: Patch Apache’s HTTP/2 Race
lede: CVE-2026-119618 can turn a race in Apache’s HTTP/2 module into heap corruption and unauthenticated remote code execution. Upgrade to 2.4.71 or later; if that is not possible, disable HTTP/2.

headline: AWS Brings The Emulator Home
lede: AWS Emulator runs AWS-compatible APIs locally, without an account, network access, or cloud charges. It targets development and CI, with service fidelity and support still varying by implementation.

headline: Reverse-Engineering A Switch 2 Dock
lede: A €40 USB-C hub becomes a portable Nintendo Switch 2 dock through USB-PD captures and firmware surgery. The build teaches the hub Nintendo’s identity checks, then patches its video converter for better HDR signaling.

headline: One Datacenter, One Dangerous False Alarm
lede: A construction-triggered smoke alarm shut down cooling at Jane Street’s only New York datacenter while sprinkler pipes pressurized. With server temperatures rising, an employee cut rack power by hand—then the firm rebuilt its monitoring around the failure.

headline: Nvidia’s Succession Question Is The Story
lede: A report that Nvidia may be preparing to remove Jensen Huang demands careful separation of allegation from evidence. Any leadership change would reach beyond one executive, testing the company’s strategy, controls, and dependence on a singular public figure.
pullquote: Nvidia’s greatest strength may also be its deepest succession risk.
